summary: Candidate leads for complementary population context. CDC SVI offers local social vulnerability measures; CDC SMART BRFSS may offer an external regional comparison if the relevant MMSA is available. Neither source was acquired in this research. The opened pages did not establish current PLACES direct download/API URLs, so those are omitted.

sources.title: CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) data download
sources.publisher: CDC / Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry
sources.geography: Selectable U.S. state or national counties and census tracts; New Jersey selection can support Middlesex County and tract-level context. New Brunswick tract coverage not independently checked.
sources.period: Selectable SVI release year; page lists documentation through 2022 and indicates ZCTA availability only for 2022.
sources.grain: Geography × SVI measure/estimate/rank; CSV table or ESRI geodatabase. Exact columns depend on selected release and geography and were not verified here.
useful_fields: Social vulnerability theme and overall measures
observed_facts: The official CDC/ATSDR download page offers CSV table and ESRI geodatabase options.
Users can select state or national ranking universes; rankings from these universes are not interchangeable.
Tribal tract data include estimates, percentages, margins of error and adjunct variables; ZCTAs are available only for 2022.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Select New Jersey, the desired SVI year, county and/or tract geography, and CSV; capture the download URL and metadata with the acquired file, preserve estimates and margins of error, and record the ranking universe. Check Middlesex County and New Brunswick coverage before modeling.
limitations: This is a candidate source, not an acquired dataset; exact file URL, columns, license terms and New Brunswick coverage were not verified.
SVI is a vulnerability/context index, not a health outcome or hospital catchment measure.
State-relative and U.S.-relative ranks answer different comparison questions.

sources.title: SMART: BRFSS City and County Data and Documentation
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.geography: Selected metropolitan/micropolitan statistical areas (MMSAs), including cities and surrounding counties where available; exact applicability to New Brunswick and Middlesex County is unverified.
sources.period: Annual SMART datasets listed for 2009–2024; selected year determines survey period.
sources.grain: SMART prevalence records by selected MMSA, measure/condition or behavior, and survey year; exact schema depends on annual dataset.
useful_fields: Selected condition and behavior prevalence rates
observed_facts: CDC describes SMART as BRFSS prevalence estimates for selected conditions and behaviors in cities and surrounding counties.
The official page lists annual data and documentation from 2009 through 2024 and directs users to year-specific documentation for weighting and calculated variables.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Check annual SMART files for an MMSA that actually includes the target geography; download one relevant year and its documentation, then retain measure definitions, year, denominator and weighting notes. If no matching MMSA exists, do not substitute its estimates for local prevalence.
limitations: No direct file URL, record fields, license evidence or matching MMSA was verified in this bounded review.
Regional survey estimates may not represent New Brunswick or Middlesex County specifically.
BRFSS survey estimates should not be treated as hospital arrival mix or patient-level data.

missing_inputs: A verified current-release PLACES endpoint and schema for a complementary slice were not established; the task reports local CDC PLACES 2025 data already acquired.
No local-to-hospital catchment mapping or patient-origin distribution was verified.
No matching SMART MMSA for New Brunswick/Middlesex County was verified.
The exact SVI release file, variables, margins of error and reuse terms require inspection at acquisition.
simulation_use: Use SVI candidate records as community-context features only after verifying geography, release, estimates, uncertainty fields and ranking universe. Use SMART only as a clearly labeled external regional benchmark if its documented MMSA coverage is relevant. Keep population context separate from hospital encounter mix and preserve reported, estimated and modeled status.
limitations: Research was limited to two searches and four primary-source page opens; listed sources are discovery leads, not acquired datasets.

The CDC page listing 2025 PLACES release notes confirms its survey and ACS reference periods, but this response does not re-audit the already acquired PLACES records or establish their confidence-interval comparison rules.
All candidate applicability, file schemas, direct download URLs and redistribution terms require independent verification before use.
